findings.title: Foundation family is selected nondeterministically
findings.body: The command uses the first OneLevelBased structural-foundation family exposing writable Length and Width parameters. A project can contain several qualifying families, including piles, pile caps, or custom footings whose geometry is not a centered rectangle driven solely by those parameters. Collector order is not a valid family-selection contract, so identical CAD input can create the wrong foundation geometry depending on project contents. Select a configured or user-approved rectangular footing family and validate its parameter/placement contract before creating instances.

findings.title: Active view level overrides the CAD elevation
findings.body: Whenever the active view has a GenLevel, every extracted foundation is associated with that level regardless of data.Center.Z. The elevation-based lookup is only used from views without a level. Running the command from a plan for another story therefore creates foundations with the wrong level association and a potentially large positive or negative offset, causing incorrect schedules and unexpected movement when levels change. Resolve the target level from each CAD center elevation, or explicitly constrain the command to and validate the active level.

findings.title: Loop discovery can freeze Revit on realistic CAD layers
findings.body: FindLoopDFS scans the complete line list at every recursion depth and recursively explores each connected alternative. Even disconnected input is quadratic, while intersections and branching linework can produce combinatorial backtracking and recursion deep enough to overflow the stack. Because the selected CAD file controls this input and execution occurs on Revit's UI thread, a dense S-FND layer can hang or crash the host. Build a tolerance-quantized endpoint adjacency map and use bounded iterative graph traversal instead of repeatedly scanning every line.
